name: I/O Linc
description: The I/O Linc, with a sensor input and a relay output.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.label: Programming lock
operatingFlags.description: Linking and programming from the device itself are locked out.

operatingFlags.name: ledOnTransmit
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED when sending
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

operatingFlags.name: relayFollowsInput
operatingFlags.label: Relay follows input
operatingFlags.description: The relay follows the sensor input.

operatingFlags.name: momentary
operatingFlags.label: Momentary relay
operatingFlags.description: The relay is momentary (momentary A): it closes for the momentary time and then opens.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay, this flag on and the momentaryOnBothCommands flag (0x10) off, a group On pulsed the relay closed when the responder record's Data 1 was 0xFF, and a group Off did nothing; with Data 1 as 0x00, a group Off pulsed it closed and a group On did nothing. A load on the relay, a driven sensor input, the momentaryFollowsSensor flag (0x80) and the relayFollowsInput flag (0x04) weren't tried.

operatingFlags.name: momentaryOnBothCommands
operatingFlags.label: Momentary on On and Off
operatingFlags.description: Both On and Off commands close the momentary relay (momentary B).

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay, this flag changed the relay's behavior only while the momentary flag (0x08) was on. With both flags on, every group On and every group Off pulsed the relay closed, whatever the responder record's Data 1 held. With the momentary flag off and this flag on, the relay latched: with Data 1 as 0x00, a group Off closed the relay and it stayed closed for over 50 seconds, and a group On changed nothing.

operatingFlags.name: triggerReversed
operatingFlags.label: Reverse the sensor
operatingFlags.description: The I/O Linc sends On when the sensor input opens rather than when it closes.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, Get Operating Flags (cmd1 0x1F, cmd2 0x00) answered with cmd2 0x5A, with the ledOnTransmit (0x02), momentary (0x08), momentaryOnBothCommands (0x10) and triggerReversed (0x40) flags set, and with 0x1A once this flag was cleared, so bit 6 holds it. With nothing connected to the sensor input, Light Status Request with cmd2 0x01 (cmd1 0x19) answered with cmd2 0x00 for the input both with this flag set and with it cleared, so the flag's effect on the sensor wasn't seen.

operatingFlags.name: momentaryFollowsSensor
operatingFlags.label: Momentary follows sensor
operatingFlags.description: Whether the momentary relay closes depends on the state of the sensor input (momentary C).

operatingFlags.name: keyBeep
operatingFlags.label: Beep on button press
operatingFlags.description: The I/O Linc beeps when its SET button is pressed.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.label: ALL-Link database changes
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

flagCommands.name: sendX10OnWhenOff
flagCommands.description: The I/O Linc sends X10 On when its input turns off.

flagCommands.name: sendX10OnWhenOn
flagCommands.description: The I/O Linc sends X10 On when its input turns on.

flagCommands.name: x10OnTurnsOff
flagCommands.description: A received X10 On turns the relay off.

flagCommands.name: x10OnTurnsOn
flagCommands.description: A received X10 On turns the relay on.

values.name: momentaryPrescaler
values.label: Momentary time multiplier
values.description: The multiplier for the momentary time. With 0x46 and a momentary time of 0xFF, the relay stays closed for about 30 minutes.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay and the momentary flag (0x08) on, the relay stayed closed for about the momentary time times this multiplier, in tenths of a second. With a momentary time of 0x64 (100), a multiplier of 0x01 held it closed for about 10 seconds and 0x02 for about 20 seconds, and 0x00 behaved like 0x01. The times were measured by polling Light Status Request (cmd1 0x19, cmd2 0x00), to within about 4 seconds.

values.name: momentaryTime
values.label: Momentary time
values.description: How long the relay stays closed in momentary mode, in tenths of a second.

values.name: x10InputHouseCode
values.label: Sensor X10 house code
values.description: The input's X10 house code, or 0x20 for no X10 address.

values.name: x10OutputHouseCode
values.label: Relay X10 house code
values.description: The output's X10 house code, or 0x20 for no X10 address.

writes.name: momentaryTime
writes.description: Sets the momentary time. A nonzero time turns the momentary flag on, and 0x00 turns it off.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, writing a nonzero momentary time turned the momentary flag (0x08) on. Turning the flag off afterwards with Set Operating Flags (cmd2 0x07) left the momentary time as written.

writes.name: momentaryPrescaler
writes.description: Sets the multiplier for the momentary time.

standardCommands.name: lightOn
standardCommands.description: Turns the output relay on. The device isn't documented to read cmd2; send 0xFF. In a momentary mode, the relay closes for the momentary time, or not at all if the mode ignores On.

parameter.name: onLevel
parameter.description: Not documented to be read; send 0xFF.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay, Light ON (cmd1 0x11) turned the relay on. With the momentary flag (0x08) on, Light ON and Light ON Fast (cmd1 0x12) closed the relay, with the momentaryOnBothCommands flag (0x10) on or off. No document gives the I/O Linc's direct commands. The Insteon Developer's Guide gives Light ON (cmd1 0x11), Light OFF (cmd1 0x13) and Light Status Request (cmd1 0x19, cmd2 0x00) for categories 0x01 and 0x02, not for the I/O Linc's 0x07, and the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual says the output relay responds to Insteon ON and OFF commands; the relay's commands are read from those.

standardCommands.name: lightOff
standardCommands.description: Turns the output relay off. In a momentary mode, the relay closes for the momentary time if the mode triggers on Off, and otherwise ignores it.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay, Light OFF (cmd1 0x13) turned the relay off. With the momentary flag (0x08) on, neither Light OFF nor Light OFF Fast (cmd1 0x14) closed the relay, with the momentaryOnBothCommands flag (0x10) on or off. No document gives the I/O Linc's direct commands. The Insteon Developer's Guide gives Light ON (cmd1 0x11), Light OFF (cmd1 0x13) and Light Status Request (cmd1 0x19, cmd2 0x00) for categories 0x01 and 0x02, not for the I/O Linc's 0x07, and the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual says the output relay responds to Insteon ON and OFF commands; the relay's commands are read from those.

standardCommands.name: readStatus
standardCommands.description: Reads whether the output relay is on. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay, Light Status Request (cmd1 0x19, cmd2 0x00) answered with cmd2 0x00 while the relay was off, and with 0xFF, a value the relay group type reads as On, while it was on. The acknowledgment's cmd1 held the ALL-Link database delta. No document gives the I/O Linc's direct commands. The Insteon Developer's Guide gives Light ON (cmd1 0x11), Light OFF (cmd1 0x13) and Light Status Request (cmd1 0x19, cmd2 0x00) for categories 0x01 and 0x02, not for the I/O Linc's 0x07, and the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual says the output relay responds to Insteon ON and OFF commands; the relay's commands are read from those.

standardCommands.name: beep
standardCommands.description: Asks the device to beep once.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: the device acknowledged Beep (cmd1 0x30), sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5. No document lists Beep for the I/O Linc.

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On or off
responder.description: 0x00 sets the relay off when the controller's On arrives, 0xFF on. A controller's Off sets the opposite state. This holds with the momentary flags off.

verification.note: Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: linked to a Hub 2245 with the momentary flag off, the device wrote its responder record with Data 1 as 0x00 when the relay was off and 0xFF when it was on. A group On, Light ON (cmd1 0x11) with the group's number, then set the relay to the recorded state, and a group Off, Light OFF (cmd1 0x13), set it to the opposite state. With the momentary flag on, the relay returned to off soon after a Light ON, before a link could finish, and the record's Data 1 was 0x00 whatever state the relay had been set to.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: sent from a Hub 2245 with modem firmware 0xA5, with nothing wired to the relay, the On action, Light ON (cmd1 0x11), turned the relay on, and the Off action, Light OFF (cmd1 0x13), turned it off. Light Status Request answered with cmd2 0x00 while the relay was off, and with a value the ranges read as On while it was on. No document gives the I/O Linc's direct commands. The Insteon Developer's Guide gives Light ON (cmd1 0x11), Light OFF (cmd1 0x13) and Light Status Request (cmd1 0x19, cmd2 0x00) for categories 0x01 and 0x02, not for the I/O Linc's 0x07, and the I/O Module 2450 Owner's Manual says the output relay responds to Insteon ON and OFF commands; the relay's commands are read from those. That every nonzero reply means on is read from Light Status Request's on-level for on/off devices, as the Insteon Developer's Guide gives it, and isn't documented for the I/O Linc.

Seen on a device running firmware 0x41: with the momentary flag on, the relay returned to off soon after a Light ON (cmd1 0x11), before a link could finish, so a link made then recorded Data 1 as 0x00 whatever state the relay had been set to. With the flag off, a link made with the relay on recorded 0xFF and one made with it off recorded 0x00.

notes: A later source marks bit 6 of the 0x00 reply as ignored; an earlier source reads it as the trigger reversal that 0x0E and 0x0F set.
An earlier source labels D5 and D6 of the reply the relay's X10 address and D7 and D8 the sensor's, where a later source has the input's and the output's.

Recording a relay state at link time needs the momentary flag off, and the relay left in the state to record. A relay wired to a door, lock or valve stays in that state until it is set back, and the momentary flag stays off until it is restored, so a flow restores both on every failure path, including cancellation.

valueTables.name: onOff
valueTables.description: Off and on, for a relay a record switches.
